name: antifungals overview
title: Antifungals decision chart: the fungus, its site and severity pick the drug. Mucosal candidiasis (nystatin, clotrimazole, fluconazole), candidemia (fluconazole for albicans, an echinocandin for severe or non-albicans), invasive aspergillosis (voriconazole or amphotericin B), cryptococcus (amphotericin B with flucytosine, then fluconazole) and endemic mycoses (itraconazole, or amphotericin B when severe), with the azole and amphotericin B harms that limit the choice

root.title: Antifungals: WHICH FUNGUS, WHERE, and HOW SICK picks the drug
lines: fungi are eukaryotes: hit what we lack, the CELL WALL (echinocandins) or ERGOSTEROL (azoles, amphotericin B)
AVOID: azoles block human CYP450 (DRUG INTERACTIONS, QT, liver) · amphotericin B: NEPHROTOXIC

head: h
Mucosal candidiasis
thrush, esophagitis, vaginitis
first: • thrush: NYSTATIN 400,000 units swish + spit QID × 7–14 days
• vaginal: clotrimazole 1% cream × 7 nights, or fluconazole 150 mg po ONCE
next: • esophagus needs SYSTEMIC: 200–400 mg po daily × 14 days

head: h
Candidemia (fungemia)
is it C. albicans?
first: 800 mg IV once, then 400 mg IV daily
next: • caspofungin 70 mg IV once, then 50 mg daily
Focus in the EYE or CNS?
echinocandins do not get there: choose another drug

head: h
Invasive aspergillosis
first: • 6 mg/kg IV q12h × 2, then 4 mg/kg IV q12h

head: h
Cryptococcal disease
in 3 phases
next: 200–400 mg po daily · lifelong may be considered

head: h
Blasto-, coccidioido-, histoplasmosis
the endemic mycoses
first: • blasto: 200 mg po TID × 3 days, then BID × 6–12 months
